'''Marcelo Vieira da Silva Júnior''' (born 12 May 1988), known as '''Marcelo''', is a Brazilian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[left-back]]. Widely regarded as one of the greatest left-backs of all time, he is known for his attacking capabilities.<ref name="lifeline" /> He spent most of his career with [[La Liga]] club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and is one of the club's [[List of Real Madrid CF records and statistics#Others|most decorated players]], winning 25 trophies.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Marcelo becomes most decorated player in Real Madrid history after La Liga title triumph {{!}} Goal.com |url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/marcelo-most-decorated-player-real-madrid-history-la-liga/blt5500917e0dc2806b |access-date=2022-04-30 |website=www.goal.com |archive-date=30 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220430170201/https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/marcelo-most-decorated-player-real-madrid-history-la-liga/blt5500917e0dc2806b |url-status=live }}</ref>

Starting his professional career with Fluminense in 2005, Marcelo won a [[Campeonato Carioca]] title in his first season and was named in the 2006 Brasileirão [[Prêmio Craque do Brasileirão|Team of the Season]]. In January 2007, he joined Real Madrid for an €8 million fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/real-madrid-signs-defender-marcelo-1.589001 |title=Real Madrid signs defender Marcelo |date=15 November 2006 |access-date=17 July 2017 |archive-date=3 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903170832/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/real-madrid-signs-defender-marcelo-1.589001 |url-status=live }}</ref> At Real Madrid, he went on to be a mainstay, winning many trophies, including five [[UEFA Champions League]] titles and six La Liga titles.<ref name=":4" /> In 2021, Marcelo became the captain of Real Madrid from the start of the [[2021–22 Real Madrid CF season|2021–22]] season, making him the first foreign captain since 1904.<ref name=":5" /> After leaving Real Madrid in 2022, he had a five-month spell at [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]], followed by a return to Fluminense in 2023, where he won the [[Copa Libertadores]]. He has been named in the [[FIFPro World XI]] six times, the [[UEFA Team of the Year]] three times, and [[La Liga Awards|La Liga's Team of the Season]] in 2016. He was also named to ''[[France Football]]''<nowiki/>'s "Team of the Decade (2010–2019)".<ref name=":6" />

Having debuted for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] in 2006, Marcelo was part of the [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Olympic squad]] and won a [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament#Bronze medal match|bronze medal]]. Four years later, he was part of Brazil's [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Olympic team]] and won a [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament#Gold medal match|silver medal]].<ref name=":0" /> Marcelo played in the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]] as Brazil was victorious, beating [[Spain national football team|Spain]] 3–0 in the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup final|final]]. He was also part of Brazil's squad at two [[FIFA World Cup]]s ([[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]] and [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]]), being named in both tournament's Dream Teams.<ref name=":1" />

==Club career==
===Fluminense===
Marcelo started playing [[futsal]] at age nine and by age 13, he was on the books of [[Fluminense Football Club|Fluminense]] in Rio de Janeiro. He came from a very poor background and even considered quitting football, but his grandfather convinced him to continue with the sport.

===Real Madrid===
[[File:MarceloRealMadrid.JPG|thumb|left|upright|Marcelo training with Real Madrid in 2007]]
Marcelo joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] during the January transfer window in 2007. On his arrival, club president [[Ramón Calderón]] said, "He is an important signing for us. He is a young player who will inject some freshness into the side and is part of our plan to bring younger players into the squad. We're very happy because he's a pearl that half of Europe wanted."<ref>[http://www.sportsnews24h.com/Soccer/Spain/Real-Madrid C.F./12069.html Brazilian Marcelo to join Real Madrid] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071217144949/http://www.sportsnews24h.com/Soccer/Spain/Real-Madrid/ |date=17 December 2007 }} SportsNews24h.com Retrieved 27 October 2007</ref> Many spectators hailed him as Brazilian and Real Madrid great [[Roberto Carlos (footballer)|Roberto Carlos]]' potential successor in the left-back role.

Marcelo made his debut as a substitute in the 2–0 defeat against [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] on 7 January 2007.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://home.skysports.com/matchreport.aspx?fxid=306162&cpid=23 |work=Sky Sports |title=Sky Sports – Football – Match Facts – Deportivo v Real Madrid – 7th January 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070114175616/http://home.skysports.com/matchreport.aspx?fxid=306162&cpid=23 |archive-date=14 January 2007 }}</ref> On 14 April 2007, then coach [[Fabio Capello]] gave Marcelo his first start for Real Madrid against [[Racing de Santander]]. Real Madrid controversially lost the game 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadridnews.com/marcelo-ten-years-success-real-madrid-19515|title=Marcelo, Ten Years of Success at Real Madrid -|last=Realmadridnews.com|date=15 November 2016|access-date=18 September 2017|archive-date=3 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903170827/http://www.realmadridnews.com/marcelo-ten-years-success-real-madrid-19515|url-status=live}}</ref> In the [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08 season]], Marcelo started nearly all of Madrid's league games under the new manager [[Bernd Schuster]]. His ability, speed running across the field, attack, and defence had enabled him to become a very important player for Real Madrid.

After a string of poor performances in 2009, Marcelo found himself on the bench for much of the remaining season while under new manager [[Juande Ramos]], mainly as deputy to the more defensive-minded [[Gabriel Heinze]]. Ramos deployed Marcelo as a winger on more than one occasion, and the Brazilian adapted well to his new role. He scored his first goal after receiving a heel flick from striker [[Gonzalo Higuaín]] and slotting the ball past the goalkeeper in Madrid's 4–0 thumping of [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]]. After the game, coach Ramos declared that Marcelo's future would be positioned as a winger, but will push back to defense when required. Marcelo scored his second goal for Real Madrid in a victory over [[UD Almería|Almería]], a powerful strike from outside the box with his weaker right foot.

On 18 April 2009, he scored his third goal of his Real Madrid career, when he scored the only goal of the game against [[Recreativo de Huelva|Huelva]] away from home.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2009/04/18/1216947/marcelo-sees-real-madrid-past-recreativo-huelva|title=Marcelo Sees Real Madrid Past Recreativo Huelva|date=18 April 2009|work=goal.com}}</ref> He scored his fourth goal against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] at the [[Estadio Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán|Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán]] in April 2009.

====2009–2011: Rise to prominence====
[[File:Marcelo in 2009-10 Real Madrid.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Marcelo with Real Madrid in 2010]]
Under the next head coach [[Manuel Pellegrini]], Marcelo consistently featured in the starting XI for his versatility and pace along the left flank in [[Offense (sports)|offensive]] and [[Defender (association football)|defensive]] roles. He continued to be employed as a left-winger under Pellegrini, and reached the top of the assist charts of La Liga in the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]]. He admitted in a press conference at the end of 2009, "I now feel better playing as a winger."<ref>[http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/encuentro-mejor-ahora-juego-extremo/dasftb/20091228dasdaiftb_22/Tes Marcelo "Me encuentro mejor ahora que juego de extremo"]. AS.com (28 December 2009). Retrieved 21 June 2012.</ref> His successful performance in Real Madrid's 2009–10 campaign earned him a contract extension on 5 February 2010 with the club until June 2015.<ref>[http://goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2010/02/05/1777837/marcelo-signs-real-madrid-contract-extension FINISHED Marcelo Signs Real Madrid Contract Extension] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100208192641/http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2010/02/05/1777837/marcelo-signs-real-madrid-contract-extension |date=8 February 2010 }}. Goal.com (5 February 2010). Retrieved 21 June 2012.</ref> This season proved to be his breakthrough season at the club.

In the [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11 season]] under new coach [[José Mourinho]], Marcelo was back in his natural position of left back. He started all league games, paying back the coach's confidence in him with defensive steel and attacking intent and gained the coach's admiration. On 25 November 2010, Marcelo was named as a part of the 55 player shortlist for the [[FIFPro|FIFA World XI]]. He scored his first goal of the new season in a 1–0 win against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] on 13 February.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en/news/745/fifa/2010/11/25/2231246/fifa-announces-55-man-shortlist-for-2010-world-xi FIFA Announces 55-Man Shortlist For 2010 World XI]. Goal.com (25 November 2010). Retrieved 21 June 2012.</ref> He had a terrific match against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] in the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]]. Showing his attacking flair and defensive skills, he opened the scoring with his first-ever Champions League goal and assisted [[Karim Benzema]]'s goal, at the end he was named man of the match, of which Real went on to win 3–0, and progressed to the quarter-finals for the first time since 2004.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/marcelo-calms-real-nerves-as-mourinho-ends-sevenyear-wait-2244053.html | location=London | work=The Independent | first=Pete | last=Jenson | title=Marcelo calms Real nerves as Mourinho ends seven-year wait | date=17 March 2011 | access-date=30 October 2017 | archive-date=25 September 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925211038/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/marcelo-calms-real-nerves-as-mourinho-ends-sevenyear-wait-2244053.html | url-status=live }}</ref> Marcelo then continued his fine season by scoring in the second leg of the semi-finals against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in the [[Camp Nou]]. The game ended 1–1, but Real Madrid lost by an aggregate score of 3–1 since they lost 2–0 at home in the first leg. Marcelo's successful campaign in the Champions League earned him a starting spot in [[UEFA]]'s starting XI. Marcelo was heavily praised by the worldwide media during that season, and many called him the best left back in the world. [[Diego Maradona]] said he was the third best player in La Liga, after [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] and [[Lionel Messi]].<ref name="autogenerated2">[http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/02/24/2366948/diego-maradona-tips-tottenham-target-sergio-aguero-to-join Diego Maradona tips Tottenham target Sergio Aguero to join Real Madrid one day] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110227130119/http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/02/24/2366948/diego-maradona-tips-tottenham-target-sergio-aguero-to-join |date=27 February 2011 }}. Goal.com (24 February 2011). Retrieved 21 June 2012.</ref>

====2011–2013: First-team mainstay====
[[File:Marcelo Vieira 609.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Marcelo training with Real Madrid in 2012]]
Marcelo was sent off on 17 August 2011 during Madrid's 3–2 loss to Barcelona. On 3 December 2011, Marcelo scored Madrid's third goal in a 3–0 victory over [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]] in [[2011–12 La Liga|La Liga]].

[[Paolo Maldini]] gave credits to Marcelo and called him the current left back, "who is a great attacker and a defender, a specialist of both areas."<ref name="autogenerated1">[http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2011/12/16/2804938/paolo-maldini-tottenhams-gareth-bale-only-knows-how-to Paolo Maldini: Tottenham Hotspur's Gareth Bale only knows how to attack] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120108024300/http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2011/12/16/2804938/paolo-maldini-tottenhams-gareth-bale-only-knows-how-to |date=8 January 2012 }}. Goal.com (16 December 2011). Retrieved 21 June 2012.</ref>

Roberto Carlos named Marcelo as the world's best left back, saying. "He had more ability than me with the ball and he joins in better," and even called him his heir.<ref name="adifferentleague1">[http://www.adifferentleague.co.uk/p6_1_14158_la-liga-headlines-roberto-carlos-marcelo-best-in-world.html La Liga Headlines: Roberto Carlos: Marcelo best in world] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331225328/http://www.adifferentleague.co.uk/p6_1_14158_la-liga-headlines-roberto-carlos-marcelo-best-in-world.html|date=31 March 2012}}. Adifferentleague.co.uk (29 March 2012). Retrieved 21 June 2012.</ref> Marcelo had shown great performances as a left back, such as in the Champions League quarter-finals against Cypriot club [[APOEL F.C.|APOEL]], while entering as a substitute in the 75th minute for [[Fábio Coentrão]]. Marcelo was part of the starting XI as Real Madrid claimed their 32nd league title.

Marcelo scored his first goal of the season against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage on 19 September, Real's first goal of a 3–2 win at the [[Santiago Bernabeu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Bevan|first=Paul|title=Real Madrid 3–2 Man City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19553991|access-date=26 May 2014|newspaper=[[BBC Sport]]|date=12 September 2012|archive-date=13 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140513071302/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/19553991|url-status=live}}</ref>

As of February 2013, Marcelo had returned from injury and captained Real Madrid on 23 February at the [[Estadio Riazor]] which ended in a 2–1 victory for ''Los Merengues''. On 20 April, he played as the captain again against [[Real Betis]] at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]]. In the 14th minute, he sustained a muscle injury after intercepting a long through-ball, but the game ended in 3–1 victory for the home side.

====2013–2018: European and domestic success====
Marcelo scored the opening goal for Real Madrid against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the Guinness International Champions Cup 2013 final on 7 August; Real Madrid won 3–1.<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid beat Chelsea 3–1 to claim the International Champions Cup|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/300010/report|access-date=26 May 2014|newspaper=[[Sky Sports News]]|date=7 August 2013|archive-date=3 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903170838/https://www.skysports.com/football/real-madrid-vs-chelsea/report/300010|url-status=live}}</ref> During the league season, he played 28 matches, and scored one goal, in a 3–0 win over [[Levante UD|Levante]] on 9 March.<ref>{{cite news|last=Jurejko|first=Jonathan|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Levante|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26489866|access-date=26 May 2014|newspaper=[[BBC Sport]]|date=9 March 2014|archive-date=23 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140523052117/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/26489866|url-status=live}}</ref>

Marcelo scored Real Madrid's third goal of their 4–1 win in the [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]] against city rivals [[Atlético Madrid]], with an extra-time strike from outside the box after coming on as a substitute for [[Fábio Coentrão]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Real Madrid 4 Atlético Madrid 1|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27383593|access-date=25 May 2014|newspaper=BBC Sport|archive-date=26 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126180206/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27383593|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:RealM-Shahter15 (7).jpg|thumb|right|220px|Marcelo in action against [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] during the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stages of the 2015–16 UEFA Champions League]]]]
On 10 July 2015, Marcelo signed a new contract with Real Madrid, keeping him at the club until 2020. On 18 October 2015, he scored his first goal of the season by scoring Real Madrid's first goal in a 3–0 home win against [[Levante UD|Levante]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/marcelo-at-real-madrid-until-2020|title=Marcelo, at Real Madrid until 2020|date=10 July 2015|access-date=10 July 2015|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612190455/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/marcelo-at-real-madrid-until-2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-announcement-marcelo|title=Official Announcement: Marcelo|date=10 July 2015|access-date=10 July 2015|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612165123/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-announcement-marcelo|url-status=live}}</ref>

He was a regular starter when the team won the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], beating Atlético Madrid again in the [[2016 UEFA Champions League Final|final]] on penalties.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|date=28 May 2016|publisher=UEFA|access-date=29 May 2016|archive-date=10 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180110225552/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2016/matches/round=2000638/match=2015789/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

He played 30 matches when Madrid won the [[2016–17 La Liga|La Liga]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.&action=history.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|date=21 May 2017|work=laliga.es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Real Madrid win La Liga title with victory at Malaga|date=21 May 2017|publisher=BBC|access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=26 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181226192537/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|url-status=live}}</ref> and was a regular starter when Madrid won the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] after defeating [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] 4–1 in the [[2017 UEFA Champions League Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|date=3 June 2017|publisher=UEFA|access-date=4 June 2017|archive-date=31 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331042605/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2017/matches/round=2000787/match=2019641/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 13 September 2017, Marcelo signed a new contract which would keep him at the club until summer 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/marcelos-contract-extension|title=Marcelo's contract extension|date=13 September 2017|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|access-date=13 September 2017|archive-date=13 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170913231948/http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/marcelos-contract-extension|url-status=live}}</ref> During the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], he made eleven appearances, while scoring three goals, with Madrid winning their third consecutive and 13th overall Champions League title after defeating [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 3–1 in the [[2018 UEFA Champions League Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/|title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick|date=26 May 2018|publisher=UEFA|access-date=28 May 2018|archive-date=27 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527203029/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2018/matches/round=2000885/match=2021711/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2018–2022: Final seasons, captaincy, and departure====
During the 2018–19 season, he made 34 appearances, winning the [[2018 FIFA Club World Cup|Club World Cup]] for the third consecutive time.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/real-madrid-win-third-successive-global-crown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181222230424/https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/news/real-madrid-win-third-successive-global-crown |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 December 2018 |title=Real Madrid win third successive global crown |publisher=FIFA |date=22 December 2018 |access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref> Later on, Marcelo made 15 appearances during the 2019–20 league season, as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga|league title]].<ref name=Liga>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season|date=17 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020|website=Marca|location=Spain|archive-date=21 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200721011320/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

He appeared sporadically in the [[2020–21 Real Madrid CF season|2020–21 season]] due to various injuries and was replaced by [[Ferland Mendy]] in the left-back position. He appeared in a total of 19 matches in all competitions as Real Madrid finished second in the [[2020–21 La Liga|league]] behind Atlético Madrid.

On 16 June 2021, it was announced that he would become the captain of Real Madrid from the start of the [[2021–22 Real Madrid CF season|2021–22 season]], as the player who had been in the first team for the longest period of time after [[Sergio Ramos]]; he was assigned the role after Ramos left, making him the first foreign captain since 1904.<ref name=":5">{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/06/17/60ca692722601d4f438b4696.html|title=Marcelo becomes Real Madrid's first foreign captain since 1904|date=17 June 2021|access-date=17 June 2021|website=marca.com|archive-date=3 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903170837/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/06/17/60ca692722601d4f438b4696.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 October 2021, Marcelo made his [[List of footballers with 100 or more UEFA Champions League appearances|100th Champions League]] appearance in a 5–0 win at [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/10/19/marcelo-makes-100th-champions-league-appearance-for-real-madrid |title=Marcelo makes 100th Champions League appearance for Real Madrid |website=Real Madrid |date=19 October 2021 |access-date=14 May 2022 |archive-date=21 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021091443/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/10/19/marcelo-makes-100th-champions-league-appearance-for-real-madrid |url-status=live }}</ref>
 
On 30 April 2022, after winning [[2021–22 La Liga|La Liga]], Marcelo became the player with most titles in the history of Real Madrid, surpassing [[Paco Gento]], with 24.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/04/30/marcelos-historic-record-24-trophies-for-real-madrid|title=Marcelo's historic record: 24 trophies for Real Madrid|website=Real Madrid|date=30 April 2022|access-date=26 May 2022|archive-date=26 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220526175933/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/04/30/marcelos-historic-record-24-trophies-for-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> On 28 May 2022, Marcelo lifted his fifth Champions League trophy after defeating Liverpool 1–0 in the [[2022 UEFA Champions League Final|final]] at the [[Stade de France]], despite not featuring in the game itself.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.as.com/soccer/champions-league-final-2022-liverpool-vs-real-madrid-live-online-goals-plays-updates-n/|title=Real Madrid wins the Champions League final against Liverpool: summary, goals, plays...|website=as.com|date=28 May 2022|access-date=28 May 2022|archive-date=28 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528224209/https://en.as.com/soccer/champions-league-final-2022-liverpool-vs-real-madrid-live-online-goals-plays-updates-n/|url-status=live}}</ref> After the final, Marcelo announced that he would leave the club after 15 years.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marcelo announces Real Madrid exit after winning Champions League final against Liverpool {{!}} Goal.com |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/marcelo-announces-real-madrid-exit-after-winning-champions-league-final-against-liverpool/blt130ef01b0ad44f8f |access-date=2022-05-29 |website=www.goal.com |archive-date=3 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903170837/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/marcelo-announces-real-madrid-exit-after-winning-champions-league-final-against-liverpool/blt130ef01b0ad44f8f |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Marcelo enhances his legendary status: 25 trophies with Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/05/29/marcelo-enhances-his-legendary-status-25-trophies-with-real-madrid|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=12 June 2022|access-date=12 June 2022|archive-date=12 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220612105751/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/05/29/marcelo-enhances-his-legendary-status-25-trophies-with-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Olympiacos ===
On 3 September 2022, Marcelo signed for [[Super League Greece]] club [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Tomaras |first1=Dimitris |title=Ολυμπιακός: "Ερυθρόλευκος" ο Μαρσέλο! (vid) |trans-title=Olympiacos: Marcelo in "red and white"! (vid) |url=https://www.gazzetta.gr/football/superleague/2147838/olympiakos-erythroleykos-o-marselo-vid |access-date=3 September 2022 |publisher=Gazzetta.gr |date=3 September 2022 |language=el |archive-date=3 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903170839/https://www.gazzetta.gr/football/superleague/2147838/olympiakos-erythroleykos-o-marselo-vid |url-status=live }}</ref> In the [[2022–23 Greek Football Cup|Greek Cup]] round of 16, he scored three goals in two matches against [[Atromitos F.C.|Atromitos]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/futebol-internacional/noticia/2023/01/11/marcelo-marca-pelo-olympiacos-e-comemora-como-cristiano-ronaldo-veja.ghtml |title=Marcelo marca pelo Olympiacos e comemora como CristianGegenaldo; veja |work=globo.com |language=pt |date=11 January 2023 }}</ref> On 18 February 2023, Marcelo terminated his Olympiacos contract, departing from the club after five months.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64690709 |title=Marcelo: Brazilian defender terminates Olympiakos contract after five months |access-date=18 February 2023 |date=18 February 2023 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]]}}</ref>

=== Return to Fluminense ===
On 24 February 2023, [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] announced the return of Marcelo to the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/times/fluminense/noticia/2023/02/24/fluminense-fecha-contratacao-do-lateral-esquerdo-marcelo-ex-real-madrid.ghtml |title=Fluminense fecha contratação de Marcelo, ex-Real Madrid: "De volta ao lugar onde tudo começou" |trans-title=Fluminense sign Marcelo, formerly of Real Madrid: "Back where it all started" |access-date=24 February 2023 |date=24 February 2023|website=Globo Esporte|publisher=[[TV Globo]]|language=pt}}</ref> He made his first appearance since his return to the club in the [[2023 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] on 5 April in a 3–1 away victory against [[Sporting Cristal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.conmebol.com/analisis-del-partido/?competition=59tpnfrwnvhnhzmnvfyug68hj&season=dbsk2r2snitn1gtnz9t292hhw&match=2zg10iqw9ky8mlg4kvn23af4k |title=Club Sporting Cristal SAC 1–3 Fluminense FC|website=CONMEBOL|publisher=FIFA|date=5 April 2023}}</ref> Four days later, Marcelo scored his first goal in his second tenure at the club with a long-range strike in a 4–1 victory against [[CR Flamengo|Flamengo]] in the second leg of the [[2023 Campeonato Carioca|Campeonato Carioca]] final. As a result, he achieved another trophy with Fluminense, the first during his second spell with the club after a 4–3 win on aggregate.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/soccer/marcelos-dream-debut-goal-and-title-at-the-maracana-18-years-on-n/ |title=Marcelo's dream debut: goal and title at the Maracanã - 18 years on|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|publisher=[[PRISA]]|date=10 April 2023 }}</ref>

On 4 November 2023, he started in the [[2023 Copa Libertadores final|Copa Libertadores final]] with Fluminense against [[Boca Juniors]] in the [[Maracanã Stadium]], which ended in a 2–1 victory after extra time, to become the 12th player to win both Champions League and Copa Libertadores titles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/futebol-internacional/noticia/2023/11/04/marcelo-entra-para-grupo-dos-que-ganharam-champions-e-libertadores-veja-lista.ghtml |title=Marcelo entra para grupo dos que ganharam Champions e Libertadores; veja lista |website=globo.com|language=pt|date=4 November 2023}}</ref>

On 2 November 2024, Marcelo left the club by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-02 |title=Marcelo: Brazilian defender leaves Fluminense as contract terminated |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp9z1107ndpo |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 6 February 2025, he announced his retirement via his social media channels.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-06 |title=Última Hora: Marcelo anuncia su retirada como jugador |trans-title=Breaking News: Marcelo announces his Retirement as a player |url=https://onefootball.com/es/noticias/ultima-hora-marcelo-anuncia-su-retirada-como-jugador-40671073 |access-date=2025-02-06 |website=OneFootball |language=es}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:ARG-BRA 2008 Olympic semi-final.jpg|thumb|right|Argentina's [[Lionel Messi]] evades Marcelo in the semi-final of the [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]].]]
Marcelo scored in his [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] debut on 5 September 2006, in a 2–0 victory against [[Wales national football team|Wales]] at [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]'s [[White Hart Lane]]. He got the ball just outside the box and shot a typical Brazilian full-back goal. Marcelo has been compared to former Brazil national team left-back [[Roberto Carlos]], who also played for Real Madrid. The two had played together during the second half of the [[2006–07 Real Madrid C.F. season|2006–07 season]] before Carlos' move to Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]].<ref name=":2">{{cite news|url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2017/02/06/how-marcelo-replaced-the-irreplaceable-roberto-carlos/|title=How Marcelo replaced the irreplaceable Roberto Carlos|last=McTear|first=Euan|date=6 February 2017|work=[[These Football Times]]|access-date=3 May 2018|archive-date=1 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401070815/https://thesefootballtimes.co/2017/02/06/how-marcelo-replaced-the-irreplaceable-roberto-carlos/|url-status=live}}</ref>

He was part of the [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's team squads#Brazil|2008 Olympic squad]] as Brazil's under-23 squad, where he won a [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament#Bronze medal match|bronze medal]].

In May 2010, he was named as one of the seven substitutes for Brazil's [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] squad.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbf.com.br/php/noticias.php?e=29&n=11190 |title=Comissão técnica da Seleção Brasileira divulga a lista complementar enviada à FIFA |date=11 May 2010 |access-date=12 May 2010 |work=CBF.com.br |language=pt |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100515030023/http://www.cbf.com.br/php/noticias.php?e=29&n=11190 |archive-date=15 May 2010 }}</ref> Although he was not called up by Brazil coach [[Dunga]], he was selected again by new coach [[Mano Menezes]] for a friendly against the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] on 10 August 2010. He was the Man of the Match for a 2–1 win in a friendly against Mexico away on 11 October 2011, as he scored the winner by dribbling past several players and then blasting the goal into the net.

He was part of Brazil's [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]] as one of the three [[List of overage players in Olympic football|overage players]], with Brazil winning a silver medal.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ma/marcelo-2.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418000044/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ma/marcelo-2.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 April 2020|title=Marcelo Bio, Stats, and Results|website=Olympics at Sports-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=31 July 2017}}</ref>

Marcelo was selected to be in [[Luiz Felipe Scolari]]'s 23-man [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup squads#Brazil|Brazil]] squad that played in the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]] on home soil.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbf.com.br/Not%C3%ADcias/2013/05/14/Felip%C3%A3o%20convocou%20os%2023%20jogadores%20para%20a%20Copa%20das%20Confedera%C3%A7%C3%B5es|title=Felipão convocou os 23 jogadores para a Copa das Confederações|language=pt|trans-title=Scolari called on 23 players for the FIFA Confederations Cup|publisher=CBF|date=14 May 2013|access-date=17 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607140113/http://www.cbf.com.br/Not%C3%ADcias/2013/05/14/Felip%C3%A3o%20convocou%20os%2023%20jogadores%20para%20a%20Copa%20das%20Confedera%C3%A7%C3%B5es|archive-date=7 June 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a starter for all of the matches, including the 3–0 victory over [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup Final|final]] on 30 June, at the [[Maracanã Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jun/30/brazil-spain-live-confederations-cup-final|title= Brazil v Spain: Confederations Cup final – as it happened|date= 1 July 2013|work= Guardian UK|access-date= 4 July 2013|archive-date= 18 June 2018|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180618075803/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jun/30/brazil-spain-live-confederations-cup-final|url-status= live}}</ref>

In the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]], which was once again played on home soil, Marcelo scored an [[own goal]] in the 11th minute of the opening game against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] on 12 June, deflecting a shot by [[Nikica Jelavić]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Brazil 3–1 Croatia|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25285029|access-date=12 June 2014|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=12 June 2014|archive-date=8 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140708110046/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/25285029|url-status=live}}</ref> It was the first goal that Brazil had conceded at the World Cup,<ref>{{cite web|title=Neymar fires Brazil to comeback victory|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=neymar-fires-brazil-to-comeback-victory-2368620.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140614052850/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=neymar-fires-brazil-to-comeback-victory-2368620.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 June 2014|publisher=FIFA|access-date=12 June 2014}}</ref> although they eventually won the match 3–1.

In May 2018, Marcelo was named in the final [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads#Brazil|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44116590|title=World Cup: Neymar named in Brazil's 23-man squad|date=14 May 2018|work=BBC Sport|access-date=27 January 2019|archive-date=19 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190419223413/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44116590|url-status=live}}</ref> He wore the captain's armband in the first match and was a starter in four of the five matches Brazil played in the competition. Brazil was eliminated by Belgium in the quarter-finals on 6 July 2018, and that was his last match with the national team. In May 2019, he was omitted from Brazil's squad for the [[2019 Copa América]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2019/05/17/5cde9af1268e3efd328b45fa.html |title=Brasil deja a Vinícius y Marcelo sin Copa América |work=Marca |location=Spain |language=es |author1=Santi Siguero |date=17 May 2019 |access-date=21 May 2019 |archive-date=24 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190524084346/https://www.marca.com/futbol/real-madrid/2019/05/17/5cde9af1268e3efd328b45fa.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Style of play==
[[File:On the day of the keeper Ochoa 04.jpg|thumb|Marcelo taking on [[Rafael Márquez]] at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]]]]
Marcelo was praised by football legends such as [[Paolo Maldini]]<ref name="autogenerated1" /> and [[Diego Maradona]],<ref name="autogenerated2" /> the latter of whom also called him the best left-back in the world. Marcelo has often been compared to fellow left-back [[Roberto Carlos]], who himself described Marcelo as his heir in 2012. Carlos also commented on Marcelo's technical skills: "Marcelo possesses a better technical ability than me."<ref name="adifferentleague1" /> Marcelo is widely regarded as one of the greatest left-backs of all time.<ref name="lifeline" /><ref name="gamebreaker" /><ref name="elite">{{Cite news |title=Marcelo finds himself among Brazil's all-time football elite |language=en |publisher=ESPN |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/club/brazil/205/blog/post/3505748/marcelo-finds-himself-among-all-time-football-elite-in-brazil |access-date=12 October 2018 |archive-date=5 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181005083442/http://www.espn.co.uk/football/club/brazil/205/blog/post/3505748/marcelo-finds-himself-among-all-time-football-elite-in-brazil |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="best">{{Cite news |title=Marcelo, the best left-back in the world {{!}} Real Madrid CF |language=en |work=Real Madrid C.F. – Web Oficial |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/marcelo-the-best-left-back-in-the-world |access-date=12 October 2018 |archive-date=3 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903170837/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/marcelo-the-best-left-back-in-the-world |url-status=live }}</ref>

Known for his attacking capabilities, Marcelo mainly played as a full-back or [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|wing-back]], but he can also play on the left wing or in [[Midfielder|midfield]].<ref name="sportskeeda">{{cite web|date=16 April 2014|title=Top 5 Full Backs who can play as Wingers/Midfielders|url=http://www.sportskeeda.com/slideshow/top-5-full-backs-who-can-play-as-wingersmidfielders|work=sportskeeda.com|access-date=14 October 2014|archive-date=15 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615135817/https://www.sportskeeda.com/slideshow/top-5-full-backs-who-can-play-as-wingersmidfielders|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="FFT100">{{cite web |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/fourfourtwos-100-best-football-players-world-2018-100-21?page=0,7 |title=FourFourTwo's 100 Best Football Players in the World 2018 |publisher=FourFourTwo |date=19 December 2018 |access-date=12 March 2019 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="lifeline" /><ref name="prosper">{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2800691/zidane-helps-marcelo-and-isco-at-real-madrid |title=Marcelo and Isco prosper at Real Madrid under Zinedine Zidane |publisher=ESPN FC |author1=Eduardo Alvarez |date=3 February 2016 |access-date=12 March 2019 |archive-date=1 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301043513/http://www.espn.com/soccer/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2800691/zidane-helps-marcelo-and-isco-at-real-madrid |url-status=live }}</ref> His movement on the ball, explosive pace, agility, and [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] skills frequently see him beat opponents in one-on-one situations with [[Dummy (football)|feints]]. He is a threat on counter-attacks, as he can penetrate the opponent's defense with deep runs or get into positions where he can receive the ball often and create goals.

Moreover, his [[Cross (football)|crossing]] ability, precise passing, and his vision also allow him to function as a secondary [[playmaker]] for his team, as he can create goalscoring chances for his teammates. While naturally left-footed, he is also adept with his right foot.{{#tag:ref|See<ref name="FFT100"/><ref name="lifeline">{{cite web }}</ref>|name="style_of_play"|group="nb"}}

Despite his ability going forward, however, the defensive side of Marcelo's game has been brought into question by pundits on occasion, who have cited his defensive abilities, work-rate, and awareness as weaknesses that are in need of improvement.<ref name="FFT100" /><ref name="lifeline" /><ref name="naivety">{{cite web |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/marcelos-defensive-naivety-could-cost-real-madrid |title=Marcelo's defensive naivety could cost Real Madrid |publisher=FourFourTwo |author1=Kiyan Sobhani |date=2 October 2015 |access-date=12 March 2019 |archive-date=11 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200411024646/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/marcelos-defensive-naivety-could-cost-real-madrid |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="untouchable">{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2818005-marcelo-previously-untouchable-but-now-out-of-favour-at-real-madrid |title=Marcelo: Previously 'Untouchable' but Now out of Favour at Real Madrid |publisher=Bleacher Report |author1=Richard Fitzpatrick |date=30 January 2019 |access-date=12 March 2019 |archive-date=30 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330181044/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2818005-marcelo-previously-untouchable-but-now-out-of-favour-at-real-madrid |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Football related business activities==
In 2017, Marcelo started investing in football clubs with his company DOZE ("Twelve"). The company became a majority shareholder of [[Campeonato Paranaense]] club [[Azuriz Futebol Clube|Azuriz]] based in [[Marmeleiro]], [[Paraná (state)|Paraná]]. In 2021, DOZE invested in the Portuguese club [[C.D. Mafra|Mafra]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://tntsports.com.br/melhorfuteboldomundo/EXCLUSIVO-Marcelo-que-ja-conta-com-dois-clubes-proprios-observa-mercado-de-grandes-clubes-brasileiros-20211227-0002.html |title=EXCLUSIVO: Marcelo, que já conta com dois clubes próprios, observa mercado de grandes clubes brasileiros |publisher=[[TNT Sports (Brazil)|TNT Sports]] |date=27 December 2021 |access-date=27 December 2021 |archive-date=27 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211227215326/https://tntsports.com.br/melhorfuteboldomundo/EXCLUSIVO-Marcelo-que-ja-conta-com-dois-clubes-proprios-observa-mercado-de-grandes-clubes-brasileiros-20211227-0002.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In October 2025, he would form his own club to compete in [[Kings League Spain]] known as Skull FC, alongside Twitch streamer Plex. Marcelo would also be on the team's inaugural roster.<ref>{{cite news |title=Marcelo debutará en la Kings League con su propio equipo: el Skull FC |url=https://www.diariocritico.com/deportes/marcelo-kings-league-equipo-skull-fc |access-date=16 October 2025 |work=Diariocrítico |language=es |date=14 October 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2008, Marcelo married his longtime girlfriend Clarice Alves. On 24 September 2009, they had their first child, a son named [[Enzo Alves]]. Their second son, Liam, was born on 1 September 2015.<ref>[http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Futebol/espanhol/0,,MUL1307272-9845,00-MARCELO+DO+REAL+VIBRA+COM+NASCIMENTO+DO+FILHO+E+O+GOL+MAIS+BONITO+QUE+MARQU.html Marcelo, do Real, vibra com nascimento do filho: ‘É o gol mais bonito que marquei’] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715070859/http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Futebol/espanhol/0,,MUL1307272-9845,00-MARCELO+DO+REAL+VIBRA+COM+NASCIMENTO+DO+FILHO+E+O+GOL+MAIS+BONITO+QUE+MARQU.html |date=15 July 2014 }} Globoesporte.com Retrieved 23 October 2009</ref>

Marcelo has many tattoos, including his shirt number and his day of birth (12) tattooed, which are both on his left arm.<ref>[http://bestsoccertattoos.com/2011-real-madrid-player-with-marcelo-tattoos-designs-photos.html#more-306 2011 Real Madrid Player With Marcelo Tattoos Designs Photos] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307215409/http://bestsoccertattoos.com/2011-real-madrid-player-with-marcelo-tattoos-designs-photos.html#more-306 |date=7 March 2016 }}. bestsoccertattoos.com</ref>

He mentioned his grandfather, Pedro Vieira, as the inspiration for his football career; his grandfather supported him financially so that he could start his career in Brazil. His grandfather died in July 2014, during the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]]; Marcelo wanted to withdraw from the tournament to attend his funeral but stayed with the Brazil team to honor his grandfather's wishes.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/marcelo-stays-camp-grandfathers-death-24438947 |title=Marcelo Stays in Camp Despite Grandfather's Death |publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |date=5 July 2014 |access-date=6 July 2014 |archive-date=6 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140706130433/http://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/marcelo-stays-camp-grandfathers-death-24438947 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 26 July 2011, Marcelo attained [[Spanish nationality law|Spanish nationality]], which allows him to be registered as an EU player rather than as a non-EU player, of which there is a strict quota allowed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Real Madrid wing-back Marcelo gains Spanish passport |url=https://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/real-madrid-wing-back-marcelo-gains-spanish-passport-1779901#popup-sso |publisher=Tribal Football |access-date=1 April 2019 |archive-date=1 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401134132/https://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/real-madrid-wing-back-marcelo-gains-spanish-passport-1779901#popup-sso |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Marcelo granted Spanish nationality |url=https://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/marcelo-granted-spanish-nationality |website=The World Game |publisher=Special Broadcasting Service |access-date=1 April 2019 |archive-date=1 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401113010/https://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/marcelo-granted-spanish-nationality |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Coerts |first1=Stefan |title=Real Madrid's Marcelo granted Spanish citizenship |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/07/26/2591508/real-madrids-marcelo-granted-spanish-citizenship |publisher=goal.com |access-date=1 April 2019 |archive-date=1 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401113012/https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/07/26/2591508/real-madrids-marcelo-granted-spanish-citizenship |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Sponsorship==
In April 2013, Marcelo was unveiled as one of [[Adidas]]' new icons for a promotional event at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Bernabéu]] store which showcased the F50 adiZero. Marcelo was joined by Real Madrid teammates [[Gareth Bale]] and [[Karim Benzema]], who also wore the Adidas brand.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.footballboots.co.uk/10944-marcelo-presented-as-adidas-icon.html|title=Marcelo Presented as adidas Icon|website=Football Boots|date=17 April 2013 |access-date=14 December 2018|archive-date=16 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016174120/http://www.footballboots.co.uk/10944-marcelo-presented-as-adidas-icon.html|url-status=live}}</ref> At the event, Marcelo said, "Throughout my career, I have achieved some of my dreams, and this is one too. Being next to these stars is fantastic. They have congratulated me, it's a great brand, and I am happy."
